summary.en: A school roof collapsed in Peshawar, killing dozens of children and a teacher and prompting authorities to order school inspections. Pakistan imposed emergency rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa amid rising tension and responded to unprovoked firing by Afghan Taliban forces along the Kurram border. The government also suspended Iran trade corridors over security and smuggling concerns. Families of the killed children are demanding justice. The conflict recorded 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Et skoletak kollapset i Peshawar, og drepte dusinvis av barn og en lærer, og førte til at myndighetene beordret skoleinspeksjoner. Pakistan innførte unntakstilstand i Khyber Pakhtunkhwa på grunn av økende spenning og reagerte på uprovokert skyting fra afghanske Taliban-styrker langs Kurram-grensen. Regjeringen suspendert også Irans handelskorridorer på grunn av sikkerhets- og smuglingsbekymringer. Familien til de drepte barna krever rettferdighet. Konflikten registrerte 1 794 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
